name: As referred to public hearing (referral report, 5 Jan 2021): 15 and 13 storeys, 163 homes, an 80-bed shelter
proponent: BC Housing with the Vancouver Aboriginal Friendship Centre Society, on City land
rezoning_path: M-1 to CD-1 (819) under the Downtown Eastside Plan
notes: From the referral report: a 15-storey wing on the lane (110 social housing homes, 25 of them supportive) and a 13-storey wing on Glen Drive (53 secured market rental homes); 14,729 m2 at FSR 6.90 on 2,134.4 m2; height to 51.0 m at the parapet above the rooftop amenity; 10 ft floor to floor; 59 vehicle and 308 bicycle spaces; about 36 trees proposed; an 80-bed shelter and a 423 m2 social enterprise; a Housing Agreement for the longer of 99 years and the life of the building; the social housing owned by BC Housing. Unit mix: the 25 supportive homes are 21 studios and 4 one-bedrooms (report); the 85 other social homes 15/35/30/5 and the 53 market rentals 15/33/5 (the application as reported by Daily Hive); the report confirms 35 two-bedroom and 5 three-bedroom homes in all. Rents: a third of the 110 social homes at the shelter rate (including all 25 supportive), a third geared to income up to HILs, a third at the low end of market; entered as 37/37/36, the rounding is assumed, and the 53 market rentals are added to the market tier. Assumptions, not from the report: the floor area is not split between residential and the shelter, so both are left blank; the setbacks are placeholders for the massing; the 15 storeys are drawn as one block although the Glen Drive wing is 13; the Community Housing Fund is the nearest program in the rule stack (the report says the partners were still seeking senior government contributions); tenure is entered as social housing although 53 of the 163 homes are market rental. The building permit (BP-2021-05332, full construction 18 Oct 2023) differs: 16 storeys (15 under the Zoning and Development By-law), 25 supportive + 87 affordable + 56 market rental + 2 townhouses = 170 homes, $55,000,000.
